title: seed minimal vendor-lite bundle and kube-adapt preflight hooks
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Motivation: Customers in highly constrained on-prem environments requested a smaller, verifiable seed bundle that can bootstrap a minimal runtime and the registry mirror in air-gapped sites. This PR introduces a 'vendor-lite' seed bundle (minimal images + deterministic manifest) and a small preflight hookset called kube-adapt that detects subtle kube-distro differences (cgroup, CRI sockets, kubelet flags) and surface actionable remediation notes.

What this PR does (single-line checklist): - Add vendor-lite bundle generation script and signed manifest; - Add deterministic index format (sha256) and delta-friendly layout; - Add kube-adapt preflight checks with remediation guidance; - Wire helm preload configmap to support minimal images and optional sidecar downloader; - Small Terraform tweak to registry IAM policy to support segmented read-only manifests for staging seeds; - Add docs and quickstart for on-prem operators.

Commits summary: 1) seed: add vendor-lite bundle generator and signing (Maya T.) 2) preflight: add kube-adapt checks and remediation messages (Maya T.) 3) helm: preload-configmap and chart values for minimal bundles (J. Cruz) 4) terraform: registry module policy for segmented manifests (A. Patel) 5) docs: vendor-lite quickstart and verification steps (M. Thompson)

Files changed (high level): - installer/scripts/seed_bundle.sh: new generator that creates a slim OCI layout, verifies checksums, and produces a signed manifest for air-gapped transfer. - installer/bundles/vendor-lite/manifest.yaml: example signed manifest with sha256 indexes and image list. - pkg/preflight/checks/kube_adapt.go: new preflight checks that inspect node environment and emit remediation hints. - helm/redwood/templates/preload-configmap.yaml: optional configmap for lightweight preload of images and CA bundles. - terraform/modules/installer/aws_registry.tf: add read-only manifest ACLs and segmented prefixes for seed staging. - docs/private-installer/vendor-lite.md: operator-facing guide and verification commands. - Makefile: new targets 'bundle-lite' and 'verify-bundle'.

Notes on implementation details: The bundle generator favors an OCI layout with a flat manifest file containing ordered image entries and sha256 checksums. The 'lite' layout purposefully omits optional utility images (sideloaders) and uses compressed, trimmed layers to keep the archive <2GB for constrained transfer scenarios. The signing step uses our existing GPG keyring; verify-bundle implements both signature and checksum validation. Kube-adapt checks are intentionally non-destructive: they only read node config and provide step-by-step remediation (e.g., mapping systemd cgroup drivers, adjusting kubelet flags, CRI socket paths).

Review & CI: Initial CI run flagged a lint error in kube_adapt.go which was fixed in commit 2; another flaky e2e (image-pull-slow) tripped on GHA runner network noise and was re-run; final CI shows all checks passing (build, unit, lint, basic e2e).

Testing performed: - Manual validate: generated vendor-lite bundle, copied to a local registry mirror, and bootstrapped a 3-node cluster in an isolated network and validated workloads start within expected thresholds. - Preflight outputs tested against three distros (Ubuntu 22.04, Rocky 9, Bottlerocket) and produced targeted remediation notes. - Terraform module change tested with terraform plan and a staging account to validate policy creation and segmented prefixes.

Backward compatibility and migration: Existing full bundles are unaffected. The installer will prefer 'vendor-lite' only when bundle_size < 2GB and operator explicitly selects the lite profile. No breaking changes to Helm chart values – new 'preload.lite' boolean toggles the behavior.

Security considerations: Signed manifests + sha256 checks reduce risk of tampered artifacts in transfer. Terraform change restricts manifest prefixes with least-privilege IAM statements. Reviewers were asked to validate key handling and signing permissions.

Release notes: Adds a 'vendor-lite' seed bundle and kube-adapt preflight checks to improve air-gapped on-prem bootstraps; operators can now generate smaller bundles and run guided remediation prior to install.

Merge: Squash merge after approvals and passing CI.
